god.text:
You are building a REAL, FUNCTIONAL Lenovo LOQ Control Center for Windows.

The current application has a good diagnostic UI, but it is stuck in READ-ONLY MODE because the previous specification was overly conservative.

CHANGE THAT.

The goal is NOT to create another hardware-monitoring mockup.

The goal is to build working controls wherever the hardware/software interface makes them realistically possible.

Do not disable an entire feature simply because one low-level implementation is uncertain.

Use a layered implementation strategy:

1. Windows-supported APIs
2. Windows command-line interfaces such as powercfg where appropriate
3. Lenovo-supported interfaces
4. Existing reputable/open-source hardware interfaces or libraries
5. Hardware-specific interfaces only when technically justified and validated
6. If a specific control genuinely cannot be implemented safely, disable ONLY that control

The application must remain safe, but safety must NOT become an excuse for leaving the application permanently read-only.

==================================================
CORE OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Turn the existing "LOQ Control Center" into a functional application with:

- Windows power-mode control
- Lenovo performance-mode control where available
- Fan monitoring
- Fan control where a supported interface exists
- CPU/GPU monitoring
- Temperature monitoring
- RPM monitoring
- Custom fan curves where supported
- Automatic profile switching
- System tray controls
- Startup behavior
- Hardware diagnostics

The application should NEVER fake hardware values or pretend a control worked when it didn't.

==================================================
VERY IMPORTANT: DO NOT STOP AT READ-ONLY MODE
==================================================

The current UI contains:

"READ-ONLY MODE"

and:

"Control unavailable"

This is NOT an acceptable final state.

Replace this architecture with capability-based controls.

For example:

If CPU/GPU monitoring works:
    Enable monitoring.

If Windows power-mode control works:
    Enable power-mode control.

If Lenovo performance-mode switching works:
    Enable it.

If fan RPM can be read:
    Enable RPM monitoring.

If manual fan control is unavailable:
    Disable ONLY manual fan control.

The UI must therefore show actual capabilities instead of putting the whole application into read-only mode.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — INVESTIGATE THE EXISTING PROJECT
==================================================

Before writing new code:

- Inspect the entire existing repository.
- Identify the current UI framework.
- Identify the current architecture.
- Identify existing hardware-detection code.
- Identify existing diagnostics code.
- Identify how BIOS/model information is being obtained.
- Identify whether any power-control implementation already exists.
- Identify TODOs and deliberately disabled controls.

Do NOT throw away working code.

Improve the existing architecture.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — WINDOWS POWER MODE CONTROL
==================================================

Implement REAL Windows power-mode switching.

This is a priority feature.

Support the available Windows power configurations/modes through an appropriate Windows-supported mechanism.

Investigate and use powercfg where appropriate.

The application should be able to:

- Detect the current power scheme/mode
- Display the current mode
- Switch between available modes
- Refresh the current state after switching
- Handle administrator-permission issues correctly
- Report errors instead of silently failing

Example UI:

POWER MODE

[ Quiet ] [ Balanced ] [ Performance ]

Current:
Performance ✓

When the user clicks a mode:

1. Execute the appropriate supported Windows operation.
2. Wait for completion.
3. Re-read the active power configuration.
4. Confirm that the change actually occurred.
5. Update the UI.

DO NOT merely change a variable in the UI.

The UI must reflect the actual Windows state.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — LENOVO PERFORMANCE MODES
==================================================

Investigate how Lenovo LOQ laptops expose their performance modes.

Potential mechanisms may include:

- Lenovo Windows services
- Lenovo ACPI interfaces
- WMI
- Lenovo-supported APIs
- Existing Lenovo software interfaces
- Existing reputable open-source implementations

Do not assume every LOQ model has the same interface.

Build:

ILenovoPerformanceController

with capability detection.

Example:

IsSupported
GetCurrentMode()
SetMode()
GetAvailableModes()

Possible modes:

- Quiet
- Balanced
- Performance

If a Lenovo-specific mode cannot be controlled on the detected machine:

DO NOT disable the entire application.

Show:

"Lenovo performance control unavailable on this model"

while keeping Windows power-mode control fully functional.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — FAN MONITORING
==================================================

Implement actual fan monitoring.

Investigate reliable sensor sources such as:

- Windows hardware interfaces
- WMI
- ACPI
- LibreHardwareMonitor-compatible approaches
- Other reputable hardware-monitoring libraries

Do not invent sensor readings.

Display:

CPU FAN
3200 RPM

GPU FAN
2900 RPM

If only one fan is exposed:

CPU FAN
3200 RPM

GPU FAN
Not available

If RPM cannot be obtained:

Fan RPM unavailable

But continue implementing every other feature.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — FAN CONTROL
==================================================

Manual fan control is a HARDWARE-SPECIFIC feature.

Do not simply declare it impossible.

First investigate actual Lenovo LOQ implementations and reputable existing projects that have successfully controlled Lenovo laptop fans.

Look for:

- Lenovo-specific fan-control mechanisms
- ACPI methods
- Embedded Controller interfaces
- Existing open-source Lenovo control applications
- Existing kernel/user-mode driver approaches
- Model-specific implementations

Study how those projects determine:

- EC address/interface
- fan mode commands
- fan speed commands
- safety limits
- model compatibility

DO NOT blindly copy arbitrary EC addresses from another laptop model.

Implement model-specific capability detection.

Architecture:

IFanController
    IsSupported
    GetFanStatus()
    SetFanMode()
    SetFanSpeed()
    SetFanCurve()

Possible states:

AUTO
QUIET
BALANCED
PERFORMANCE
CUSTOM

If manual fan control is unsupported:

Disable ONLY the manual fan-control controls.

Do NOT disable:

- monitoring
- profiles
- Windows power modes
- Lenovo performance modes
- system tray
- diagnostics

==================================================
PHASE 6 — SAFE HARDWARE CONTROL
==================================================

Safety requirements still apply.

However, safety should mean:

"Validate before executing"

NOT:

"Never implement hardware control."

Before sending a hardware command:

- Verify exact laptop/model compatibility.
- Verify the interface is available.
- Validate the requested value.
- Apply reasonable limits.
- Handle failures.
- Log the operation.
- Confirm the resulting state where possible.

Never:

- Write arbitrary values to unknown EC addresses.
- Use random memory addresses.
- Disable thermal protection.
- Modify BIOS firmware.
- Disable Windows security features.
- Install suspicious software.
- Download unknown drivers automatically.

If a kernel driver is required for a legitimate, model-compatible implementation:

Explain why it is required.

Keep the driver minimal.

Keep user-mode and kernel-mode functionality separated.

Do not silently install it.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — FAN CURVE
==================================================

Build a REAL interactive fan-curve editor.

Example:

Temperature       Fan

40°C              20%
50°C              25%
60°C              35%
70°C              50%
80°C              70%
85°C              85%
90°C              100%

UI:

- Graph
- Draggable points
- Add point
- Delete point
- Reset
- Apply
- Save profile
- Load profile

Before applying:

Validate:

- Temperature ordering
- Fan percentage range
- Minimum fan level
- Maximum fan level
- Hardware-supported values

If custom curves are unsupported by the hardware:

Display:

"Custom fan curves are not supported by this model."

Do not fake them.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — PROFILE SYSTEM
==================================================

Create actual profiles.

QUIET

- Low-noise Windows power configuration
- Lenovo Quiet mode if available
- Conservative fan behavior

BALANCED

- Normal Windows power configuration
- Lenovo Balanced mode if available

PERFORMANCE

- High-performance Windows configuration
- Lenovo Performance mode if available
- More aggressive cooling

CUSTOM

- User-defined configuration

A profile must actually execute its configured actions.

Do not make profile buttons that only modify UI state.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — CAPABILITY SYSTEM
==================================================

Replace the current global:

READ-ONLY MODE

with a capability system.

Example:

SYSTEM CAPABILITIES

✓ CPU monitoring
✓ GPU monitoring
✓ Battery monitoring
✓ Windows power control
✓ Lenovo performance mode
✓ Fan RPM monitoring
⚠ Manual fan control
⚠ Custom fan curve

Each capability must independently determine:

Supported
Unsupported
Error
Requires administrator
Not detected

The application should still expose all supported controls.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — MAIN DASHBOARD
==================================================

Redesign the current dashboard.

Current UI is visually good but too diagnostic-oriented.

Make it an actual control center.

Top:

LOQ CONTROL CENTER

Model:
83DV / actual detected model

Current Profile:

PERFORMANCE

Main cards:

CPU
63°C
48%
4.1 GHz

58°C
72%
2.1 GHz

FANS

CPU
3200 RPM

2900 RPM

POWER MODE

[ Quiet ] [ Balanced ] [ Performance ]

PERFORMANCE PROFILE

[ Apply ]

==================================================
PHASE 11 — FAN CONTROL SCREEN
==================================================

Create a dedicated page:

FAN CONTROL

CPU FAN
3200 RPM

GPU FAN
2900 RPM

Mode:

[ AUTO ]
[ QUIET ]
[ BALANCED ]
[ PERFORMANCE ]
[ CUSTOM ]

If supported:

CUSTOM FAN CURVE

Interactive graph.

Apply button.

The Apply button must perform the actual hardware operation.

After applying:

Read the state again.

Show:

✓ Fan configuration applied

or:

✕ Fan configuration failed

Never say "Applied" merely because the button was clicked.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — POWER CONTROL SCREEN
==================================================

Create:

POWER & PERFORMANCE

Current Windows Power Mode:

● Performance

Buttons:

[ Quiet ]
[ Balanced ]
[ Performance ]

Lenovo Mode:

● Performance

Buttons:

[ Quiet ]
[ Balanced ]
[ Performance ]

Show the source:

Windows Power Configuration
Lenovo Performance Interface

This lets the user understand what each control actually changes.

==================================================
PHASE 13 — SYSTEM TRAY
==================================================

System tray menu:

LOQ CONTROL CENTER

CPU 63°C
GPU 58°C

Power:
Performance

Profile:
Performance

----------------

Quiet
Balanced
Performance

----------------

Tray controls must perform real actions.

==================================================
PHASE 14 — ERROR HANDLING
==================================================

Hardware failures must not crash the application.

Example:

Fan control failed.

Reason:
"Required Lenovo hardware interface was not available."

Buttons:

[ Retry ]
[ Diagnostics ]

Do not show stack traces to normal users.

Put detailed errors into logs.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — ADMINISTRATOR HANDLING
==================================================

Determine which features require administrator privileges.

Do NOT run the entire application as administrator unnecessarily.

Use the minimum privilege necessary.

If a specific operation requires elevation:

Explain it clearly.

Example:

"Fan control requires elevated privileges on this model."

[ Allow ]

Do not silently elevate.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — DIAGNOSTICS
==================================================

Keep the existing diagnostics page, but turn it into a useful engineering tool.

Show:

Laptop model
BIOS version
Windows version
CPU
GPU
Available sensor interfaces
Available Lenovo interfaces
Available power-control mechanisms
Fan-control capability
Administrator status
Driver status

Example:

✓ Lenovo LOQ detected
✓ Windows power control
✓ CPU telemetry
✓ GPU telemetry
✓ Fan RPM
✓ Lenovo performance mode
⚠ Manual fan control unavailable

Add:

[ Refresh ]
[ Export Diagnostic Report ]

==================================================
PHASE 17 — IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT RULE
==================================================

DO NOT STOP DEVELOPMENT BECAUSE ONE HARDWARE INTERFACE IS UNKNOWN.

If fan control is difficult:

Continue implementing:

- Windows power modes
- Lenovo performance modes
- monitoring
- profiles
- tray
- startup
- diagnostics
- notifications

Then continue researching and implementing fan control separately.

The final application should NEVER be intentionally crippled into read-only mode merely because manual fan control has not yet been solved.

==================================================
PHASE 18 — RESEARCH RULE
==================================================

When you encounter an undocumented Lenovo interface:

Do not immediately conclude:

"Unsupported."

Instead:

1. Search the existing codebase.
2. Search reputable public documentation.
3. Search established open-source projects.
4. Compare implementations for the same Lenovo generation/model.
5. Determine whether the mechanism applies to the detected model.
6. Implement behind a hardware-specific adapter.
7. Add capability detection.
8. Test safely.
9. Fall back gracefully if unavailable.

Do not fabricate an implementation.

Do not fabricate compatibility.

But also do not give up prematurely.

==================================================
PHASE 19 — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

The project is NOT complete if the UI only displays:

"READ-ONLY MODE"

The minimum functional release must have at least:

✓ Real hardware/model detection
✓ Real CPU/GPU/battery telemetry where available
✓ Real Windows power-mode switching
✓ Real profile switching
✓ System tray
✓ Persistent settings
✓ Diagnostics
✓ Logging
✓ Capability detection

Then implement:

✓ Lenovo performance mode switching where supported
✓ Fan RPM monitoring where supported
✓ Manual fan control where supported
✓ Custom fan curves where supported

==================================================
FINAL RULE
==================================================

Build a REAL application.

Do not create fake buttons.

Do not create fake sensor values.

Do not create fake fan control.

Do not disable functionality simply because the hardware interface requires investigation.

Use this decision:

SUPPORTED → IMPLEMENT IT

SUPPORTED WITH PRIVILEGES → IMPLEMENT IT WITH PROPER ELEVATION

MODEL-SPECIFIC → IMPLEMENT WITH MODEL DETECTION

UNKNOWN → INVESTIGATE

UNSUPPORTED → DISABLE ONLY THAT FEATURE

UNSAFE → DO NOT IMPLEMENT

Never use:

"Everything is read-only for safety"

as a substitute for engineering.

The application should be safe AND functional.

This is the new security, send to all workers
